main_body: Tall dark grey standing stone slab (about 12px wide, rows 6-31) with cyan rune glyphs on the front face
top_band: Mid-grey band at rows ~7-10, full width of the stone with only chamfered corners, about 4 rows. It reads as a flat cap rather than a surface seen from above. Below it the dark front face starts at about row 11.
evidence: In the centre column there is a short grey cap band, then a dark face with flat runes. The band is a straight rectangle with clipped corners, like the red 'flat band cap' column in the guide, not the elliptical cap of the green column. The step to the face is a single dark row with no distinct front-edge highlight and no eave shadow. The runes are painted flat on the face. The result is a front elevation with a hat, not a 3/4 object.

style.evidence: The body is mostly flat dark grey and the cap is one flat mid-grey, so only 3-4 lightness steps carry the stone. The outline is a uniform near-black line all round, which gives the sticker look. There is no grain, chipping or per-stone variation, and large areas of the face are a single flat colour. Next to the cheese stall and the roofed well, which have many tones and textured materials, most tiles here hold only 2-4 colours.
